title.narrative: Community-Based Recovery and Stabilization Project for the Sahel

description.narrative: The development objective of this project is to contribute to the recovery and resilience of communities in target areas of the Liptako-Gourma Region of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger through a regional approach supporting (i) integrated socio-economic services and infrastructure, (ii) livelihoods and territorial development, and (iii) regional data and coordination.

The project seeks to contribute to the recovery and resilience of communities in target areas of the Liptako-Gourma Region of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger through a regional approach supporting (i) integrated socio-economic services and infrastructure, (ii) livelihoods and territorial development, and (iii) regional data and coordination. The project is structured around four main components. Component 1: Resilient and inclusive recovery of conflict-affected communities. This component will not be financed under the AF, as it focuses on post-humanitarian support in less secure areas. The Government will instead prioritize scaling up durable solutions under the Community Driven Development (CDD) approach as part of Component 2 in order to sustain and build upon gains in more secure areas by building on an established delivery system capable of implementing community-responsive investments at scale. Component 2: Transitional support towards stabilization and territorial development of communities. Under this component, the AF will finance community-prioritized socio-economic infrastructure and livelihood activities in secured communities through the CDD approach. Investment options follow a consolidated open menu (subject to a negative list) including drinking water systems, sanitation, schools, health centers, solar electrification, rural markets, grain storage, irrigated perimeters, and livelihood activities. Component 3: Regional dialogue, coordination and data and capacity building. This component strengthens regional collaboration and local capacity to address FCV drivers. Sub-components 3a and 3b will not receive additional financing under the AF, as the original financing envelope remains sufficient to support regional dialogue, knowledge sharing, and exchanges among participating countries. The AF will only finance Sub-component 3c: Local-level capacity building, citizen engagement, and social inclusion, which funds locally recruited facilitators, community management committee capacity building, and the Local Development Portal for real-time coordination of local development plans. Furthermore, Component 4 supports the Project Management of the AF and Component 5 is a Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).
